subject: Data retention exception - Finova / next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Data retention exception - recap and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo and discussion today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

- Ask we heard: Finova requires tighter controls around PII and session logs for your customer-facing flows (zero retention for identified PII; shortened debug logs).
- Proposed exception: Redwood to implement zero-retention for any fields you mark as PII at ingestion time, retain ephemeral debug logs for up to 24 hours (encrypted and access-controlled), and keep aggregated metrics for 90 days.
- Data residency: requests were for US-only (us-east-1).
- Compliance: you asked for SOC 2 report and a DPA amendment reflecting the exception.

Next steps:
1) I'll circulate a DPA amendment and a short sheet that outlines the exact retention windows and technical controls (attached draft).
2) Marissa (legal/ops) will review for contract language and confirm if we can commit to 0-retention obligations and the 24-hour debug window.
3) If agreed, we’ll route the amendment for signature and schedule a follow-up to confirm ingestion mapping (so we can identify PII fields).

Can you confirm the list of PII types/fields you want zero-retention applied to and whether there are any other residency constraints? Also confirm whether the 24-hour debug window is acceptable for your SRE/debug needs.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0173

Attachments: DPA_redwood_finova_draft.pdf; redwood-data-retention-exception-sheet.xlsx

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finova.com>, Finova Legal <legal@finova.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception - recap and next steps

Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed: Finova requires zero retention for any direct PII that can identify an end user (full name + email, SSN, payment instrument data). We will provide a field mapping by Monday.
- Debugging: 24 hours for raw request/response logs would be fine for most flows, but we need the option to request extended access (up to 7 days) for specific incidents via a formal access request ticket (audited).
- Residency: us-east-1 only is a hard requirement.
- Compliance: please provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report and an updated DPA with the amendment language.

Assuming your legal can sign up to the above, we’re prepared to move forward. Also, can you confirm whether request-level metadata (IP, user-agent) would be considered PII under this exception if it can be correlated to a user? We prefer to treat correlatable metadata as PII for our environment.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Security, Finova
alex.johnson@finova.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Data retention exception - quick internal note

Camila —

Quick internal note following Alex's reply:
- Legal: I can take first pass on the DPA amendment. We should be conservative on "correlatable metadata" language; propose we explicitly list "IP address, user-agent" as configurable — customers can opt-in to treat as PII, and we’ll document access controls and audit trail requirements.
- Access requests: Agree to a ticketed process for extending retention for incidents (7 days max) with SOC/CSO approval and logged justification.
- Residency: We can commit to us-east-1 for Finova under Private/Dedicated or via hosted region controls — ops to confirm deployment model and if any cross-region backups occur.

I'll coordinate with Rafael on ops implications and update the draft. We should also confirm whether the customer expects encryption-in-transit + at-rest key management via their KMS.

Marissa
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@finova.com>, Finova Legal <legal@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception - proposed amendment and next steps

Alex / Priya —

Attached is an updated DPA amendment and a short spreadsheet that maps the proposed retention behavior by field (see attachment). Proposed summary:
- Zero retention: fields labeled as PII in your ingestion mapping (you provide the mapping) — immediate purge post-processing, no persistent raw copy.
- Debug logs: raw request/response logs retained for 24 hours by default; access can be extended to 7 days for incident investigation via a documented, auditable request process (Redwood SOC/CSO sign-off).
- Correlatable metadata (IP, user-agent): treat as PII if Finova marks them as PII in the mapping — otherwise retained as ephemeral metadata for 24 hours and stored as aggregated metrics beyond that window.
- Residency: Data processed and stored in AWS us-east-1 exclusively. No cross-region backups for this customer.
- Security: default encryption in transit and at rest; we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private deployments — note in amendment.

If this aligns, next steps:
1) Finova to send ingestion mapping of fields to designate PII.
2) Legal teams to review and redline the attached DPA amendment.
3) I will create the contract amendment/DocuSign envelope once redlines are cleared.

Can you confirm acceptance of the above summary or flag anything that looks off?

Best,
Camila

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finova.com>, Finova Legal <legal@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception - proposed amendment and next steps

Camila / Marissa —

This looks good and aligns with our expectations. We will:
- Send the ingestion mapping by EOD Monday with PII field designations.
- Finova Legal will provide any redlines to the DPA amendment; otherwise, approve.

Please proceed to generate the DocuSign amendment and include the SOC 2 Type II report and the instructions for submitting incident extension requests. Our procurement team will need the DocuSign link and a contact for any security questionnaire follow-ups.

Thanks — looking forward to moving ahead.

— Alex
